text: FDA-approved total hip arthroplasty is medically necessary for adults with advanced hip joint disease shown by (a) pain/functional disability from osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis, (b) limited passive range of motion, antalgic gait, and pain on exam, and (c) either AVN with stage II/III disease or moderate-to-severe osteoarthritis/RA at Tonnis grade 2-3; AND a documented history of 12-24 weeks of unsuccessful conservative therapy (anti-inflammatories, flexibility/strengthening exercises, activity modification, supervised in-person PT, assistive devices, and therapeutic injections as applicable) unless conservative therapy is clinically inappropriate and the record explains why. THA is also medically necessary (independent of the criteria above) for femoral neck fracture, malunion/nonunion of hip fracture with pain, or malignancy of the joint/pelvis/proximal femur.

text: THA is experimental/investigational/unproven for indications outside the criteria above, because supporting evidence of effectiveness is insufficient. Total joint replacement is not medically necessary where an absolute contraindication is present (active joint/systemic infection, active skin infection or open wound at the surgical site, implant-component allergy, recent intra-articular corticosteroid injection within 12 weeks, paraplegia/quadriplegia, permanent muscle weakness without pain preventing ambulation, rapidly progressive neurologic disease absent a concomitant fracture, or skeletal immaturity). Separately, removal/revision for post-THR metallosis alone -- without imaging evidence of loosening or malposition -- is considered experimental/investigational because peer-reviewed evidence is insufficient.

text: Facility-based nocturnal polysomnography (NPSG) is medically necessary for children/adolescents under 18 for several listed indications, most centrally to diagnose OSAS and distinguish it from primary snoring, as well as for suspected hypersomnia, narcolepsy, parasomnia, restless leg syndrome, periodic limb movement disorder, congenital central alveolar hypoventilation, or sleep-related hypoventilation from neuromuscular disease/chest-wall deformity. A repeat post-adenotonsillectomy NPSG is medically necessary (after a 6-8 week delay) for high-risk children (under age 3, cardiac complications of OSAS, craniofacial anomalies, failure to thrive, certain neuromuscular disorders, obesity, prematurity, recent respiratory infection, pre-op respiratory disturbance index >=19) or when symptoms persist post-treatment. PAP titration may be combined with the diagnostic NPSG as a split-night study if moderate/severe OSA is confirmed and adequate titration is achieved within the defined time window; otherwise a second night is required.

text: CPAP/APAP (with or without pressure-relief technology) is medically necessary DME for adults with a positive facility-based or qualifying home sleep test, defined as an AHI/RDI >=15 events/hour (minimum 30 events), OR an AHI/RDI of 5-14 events/hour (minimum 10 events) plus at least one of: documented stroke history, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, impaired cognition/mood/insomnia symptoms, excessive daytime sleepiness (Epworth >10), or significant oxygen desaturation on the sleep study. BiPAP/DPAP/VPAP without a backup-rate feature is medically necessary for members who are CPAP/APAP-intolerant or for whom it is ineffective, once proper mask fit and pressure titration have been tried and documented to fail. Jaw realignment surgery (hyoid myotomy/suspension, mandibular osteotomy, genioglossal advancement) is medically necessary only after other treatment approaches for OSA have failed.

text: Non-FDA-approved hypoglossal nerve neuro-stimulation systems (e.g., the Apnex HGNS System, aura6000, ImThera's Targeted Hypoglossal Neuro-stimulation Therapy, WellStar) are experimental/investigational/unproven for adult OSA. FDA-approved hypoglossal nerve stimulation (e.g., Inspire II/3028, Genio HGNS) is medically necessary only when all of a defined set of criteria are met: age >=18, BMI <40, PSG within 24 months, predominantly obstructive events, AHI 15-100, documented CPAP failure or intolerance, absence of complete concentric palatal collapse on DISE/laryngoscopy, and no anatomic finding that would compromise device performance.

text: Bariatric surgery (RYGB, sleeve gastrectomy, BPD +/- DS, LASGB, SADI-S, or sleeve+SIPS) is medically necessary for adults with BMI >=40 (>=37.5 for persons of Asian ancestry), OR BMI >=35 (>=32.5 Asian ancestry) plus a qualifying severe comorbidity (clinically significant OSA meeting CPB-0004 criteria, coronary heart disease, medically refractory hypertension, type 2 diabetes, or MASH), OR for adolescents who have completed bone growth with BMI >40. The member must have a documented history of unsuccessful weight-loss attempts AND documented participation in an intensive multicomponent behavioral intervention (>=12 sessions on separate dates within 2 years pre-surgery, covering nutrition, physical activity, and behavioral modification) -- program records (e.g., Weight Watchers, Jenny Craig) may substitute for medical-record documentation. A behavioral-health assessment for psychosocial functioning, substance use, and maladaptive eating is also required, with referral/treatment of any issues identified.

text: Conversion to sleeve gastrectomy, RYGB, or BPD/DS is medically necessary where the primary bariatric procedure was medically necessary but produced inadequate success (sustained loss of <50% of excess body weight) 2+ years post-op, with the member compliant with a prescribed nutrition/exercise program. Revision for pouch or gastrojejunal-stoma/anastomosis dilation is medically necessary when the primary procedure initially induced weight loss before the dilation occurred and the member remained compliant post-op. Conversion from an adjustable band to sleeve/RYGB/BPD-DS is medically necessary for members compliant with their post-band program who have complications not correctable by band manipulation, adjustment, or replacement.

policy_title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT) of the Spine
text: MRI and CT of the spine are medically necessary when any of a defined list of clinical indications is met, including: clinical evidence of spinal stenosis; suspected cord/cauda equina compression; congenital spinal anomalies; lumbar epidural lipomatosis; recurrent symptoms after spinal surgery; pre-epidural-injection planning; suspected spinal malignancy or infection (initial or follow-up); suspected myelopathy where brain MRI is negative; primary spinal cord or bone tumors; radiculopathy with objective motor/reflex findings unresponsive to 6 weeks of conservative therapy; progressively severe symptoms despite conservative management; rapidly progressing neurologic deficit; severe back pain requiring hospitalization; spondylolisthesis/degenerative disease unresponsive to 4 weeks of conservative therapy; suspected infection, trauma-related cord injury, or fracture/dislocation with inconclusive plain films; and suspected transverse myelitis. Precertification may be required depending on the specific procedure and member plan.

policy_title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the Breast
text: Annual breast MRI screening (as an adjunct to, not a replacement for, mammography performed within the past year) is medically necessary for women at elevated genetic/lifetime risk, including confirmed or first-degree-relative carriers of BRCA1/BRCA2, PTEN, TP53, PALB2, STK11/LKB1, CDH1, NF1, ATM, CHEK2, NBN, BARD1, RAD51C, or RAD51D mutations (with gene-specific starting ages ranging 20-40), and women with a calculated lifetime breast-cancer risk of 20-25% or greater under a standard risk model (BRCAPRO, Claus, Gail, or Tyrer-Cuzick). It is also medically necessary for individuals who received chest radiation between ages 10-30 (e.g., for Hodgkin disease), and for a defined set of diagnostic indications (tumor staging, implant-rupture detection, occult primary localization, inconclusive mammography/ultrasound findings, etc.).

policy_title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the Breast
text: Breast MRI is experimental/investigational/unproven (not medically necessary) for average-risk screening, and for women with dense breasts and/or fibrocystic disease who are asymptomatic with no additional risk factors -- consistent with ACOG's position that evidence is insufficient to recommend routine supplemental imaging for dense breasts absent validated outcome data. Also excluded/experimental: screening in APC-, GALNT12-, or MUTYH-mutation carriers, screening BRCA-positive men, evaluating suspicious BI-RADS 4/5 findings (which should be biopsied instead), and several other listed uses (fat-necrosis diagnosis, quantitative density measurement, chemotherapy-response prediction, etc.).

policy_title: Quantitative, Functional and Connectomic Analysis of Brain MRI
criterion_name: fMRI pre-surgical mapping (narrow indication; policy also covers quantitative/connectomic MRI analysis)
text: Functional MRI (fMRI) is medically necessary specifically to identify the eloquent cortex in pre-surgical evaluation of patients with brain tumors (except temporal tumors), epilepsy (except temporal neocortical epilepsy), or vascular malformations. This is a narrow pre-surgical planning indication, not general brain imaging. The same CPB additionally addresses automated quantitative brain MRI analysis and connectomic analysis of multi-modal brain MRI, both of which are classified as experimental/investigational/unproven rather than medically necessary.

text: FDA-approved total knee arthroplasty is medically necessary for adults with advanced knee joint disease shown by (a) pain/functional disability from osteoarthritis, RA, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis, (b) limited ROM, crepitus, or effusion/swelling on exam, and (c) radiographic evidence of Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3-4 osteoarthritis, AVN of the tibial/femoral condyle, or RA joint-space narrowing; AND a documented history of 12-24 weeks of unsuccessful conservative therapy (anti-inflammatories, flexibility/strengthening exercises, activity modification, supervised in-person PT, assistive devices, and therapeutic injections as applicable), unless clinically inappropriate and explained in the record. TKA is also medically necessary for failed prior osteotomy, distal femur/proximal tibia malunion or fracture/nonunion, malignancy of the distal femur/proximal tibia/knee/adjacent soft tissue, or failure of a prior unicompartmental replacement -- each with pain interfering with ADLs. Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty has parallel, single-compartment-specific criteria (intact ligaments, arc of motion >90 degrees, single-compartment Kellgren-Lawrence 3-4).

text: Computer-assisted/robotic surgical navigation (e.g., MAKOplasty) for knee arthroplasty is experimental/investigational/unproven because reliable evidence that it improves surgical outcomes is lacking; when used, robotic assistance is considered integral to the primary procedure and is not separately reimbursed. Other items classified experimental/investigational/unproven in this CPB include bacteriophage therapy for peri-prosthetic joint infection, bicompartmental/bi-unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, custom cutting-block instrumentation, customized implants, genicular-nerve radiofrequency ablation, mineralized-collagen bone cement, prophylactic post-TKA radiation therapy, 'smart' knee implants, and tele-rehabilitation after TKA.
